answers.solution:
I diagnosed the problem class and built a verified, self-contained solution at `/workspace/solution/`:

- `SOLUTION.md` — the full write-up
- `tools/run_pytest_arm.sh` — the fixed pytest arm wrapper
- `tests/test_run_pytest_arm.sh` — hermetic regression (passes)
- `gate/run_gate.sh` — wires the regression into the gate

## Root cause

The 1200 s budget signalled only the `pytest` process, not the process group. On a loaded host, a stalled test's descendants (xdist workers, servers, lock holders) either ignore `SIGTERM` and survive, or the gate parent dies and takes the budget owner with it — so orphans and locks leak and wedge the next run (REVIEW-AUGER-005 class).

## Fix (core)

```bash
PYTEST_BUDGET_SECS="${AUGER_PYTEST_BUDGET_SECS:-1200}"
PYTEST_KILL_AFTER_SECS="${AUGER_PYTEST_KILL_AFTER_SECS:-30}"
ARM="pytest"
tmp="$(mktemp -d)"; pgid_file="$tmp/pgid"; trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT

# new session/PGID survives the gate parent; timeout owns the budget
setsid --wait bash -c '
  echo "$$" > "$1"; shift
  exec timeout --signal=TERM --kill-after="$1" "$2" python -m pytest "${@:3}"
' _ "$pgid_file" "$PYTEST_KILL_AFTER_SECS" "$PYTEST_BUDGET_SECS" "$@" &
child=$!; set +e; wait "$child"; rc=$?; set -e

if [[ "$rc" -eq 124 || "$rc" -eq 137 ]]; then
  pgid="$(cat "$pgid_file")"
  kill -TERM -- "-$pgid" 2>/dev/null || true; sleep 1
  kill -KILL -- "-$pgid" 2>/dev/null || true
  printf 'GATE-FAIL arm=%s reason=wall-budget-exceeded budget=%ss kill-after=%ss rc=%s\n' \
    "$ARM" "$PYTEST_BUDGET_SECS" "$PYTEST_KILL_AFTER_SECS" "$rc" >&2
  exit 124
fi
exit "$rc"
```

## Verification (actually run)

```
$ timeout 60 bash tests/test_run_pytest_arm.sh
ok: TERM-ignoring grandchild 302 was killed
wrapper output: GATE-FAIL arm=pytest reason=wall-budget-exceeded budget=1s kill-after=1s rc=137
PASS test_run_pytest_arm
TEST_RC=0
```

Also verified:
- Gate self-test runs first, then the real arm succeeds (`GATE_RC=0`).
- Exit codes pass through untouched (`0` on pass, `3` on real failure) — only a budget trip becomes `124`.
- After `SIGKILL` of the wrapper, the detached `setsid` budget owner stayed alive (`t=2 yes`) and exited on its own (`t=6 no`), proving the budget survives parent death.
- `shellcheck -S warning` clean.

Full root-cause analysis, the Python gate variant, the regression code, the gate wiring, acceptance-criteria mapping, and rollout notes are in `/workspace/solution/SOLUTION.md`.
